decisive_items: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)
Admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes
T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample
response.rationale: The clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements in skin and bone marrow, along with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate, confirm a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. The CD8-positive, CD4-negative phenotype is atypical for Sézary syndrome or classic mycosis fungoides, making the broader CTCL diagnosis most appropriate.

rejected.why: Sézary syndrome is typically CD4-positive with erythroderma and leukemic involvement; the CD8-positive, CD4-negative phenotype and lack of these features make it unlikely.
Mycosis fungoides classically shows CD4-positive helper T-cells; the robust CD8 signal and CD4-negative phenotype are atypical, making the broader CTCL diagnosis more accurate.
